Fidelity evidence beyond the exit code: I ran the unmodified source twice in a scratch venv - once with the pristine loader + live network, once with the offline adapter + network blocked - and all four endpoint CSVs were byte-identical between the runs; the controller's artifact hashes (hrv_time.csv 7ed134df..., hrv_frequency.csv b9de64f3..., hrv_nonlinear.csv a2306344..., hrv_all_domains.csv 930151b9...) match those rehearsal hashes exactly. analysis.py is byte-identical to the frozen converted original (sha256 ca70f419..., zero diff), so no computation, parameter, seed or filtering change was made; runtime was ~3 s and ~220 MiB peak RSS. Executed observations resolving the preparation's open questions: hrv_time is 1x25, hrv_freq 1x10 (normalize=True), hrv_nonlinear 1x60, hrv_indices 1x95 (= 25+10+60, single-level integer index, metric-name columns, no RQA columns since peaks comes from ecg_peaks without RSP channels, so no RSA indices). All frames are populated but some columns are NaN by design of NeuroKit 0.2.13: HRV_ULF, HRV_SDANN2, HRV_SDNNI2, HRV_SDANN5, HRV_SDNNI5 are empty in the exported CSVs (ULF is not defined for a 5-min recording; the 2-/5-min segment indices likewise), matching what the notebook itself would display.
source_adaptations: No change to analysis.py: it is byte-identical to the converted original, including imports, narrative comments and all show=True plotting calls; headless rendering is provided by the controller's MPLBACKEND=Agg (matplotlib 3.11.2 also selects Agg by default in this image when no DISPLAY is present, verified without the variable set).

Offline data access (the only necessary adaptation): the notebook gets its input via nk.data("bio_resting_5min_100hz"), and NeuroKit's data() hard-codes an HTTPS GitHub URL, so it cannot run offline. stage-inputs.sh downloads the dataset from its recorded upstream provenance (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neuropsychology/NeuroKit/master/data/bio_resting_5min_100hz.csv, sha256 6a33ff8a..., byte-identical at revision ff419d98...), checksum-verifies it, and stages it at /inputs/bio_resting_5min_100hz.csv.

Offline data-loader adapter (declared in inputs.json as /work/cache/neurokit2-data/data.py): stage-inputs.sh embeds verbatim a copy of neurokit 0.2.13's neurokit2/data/data.py whose only change is that the dataset base location is resolved at call time - NEUROKIT_DATA_PATH if set, else the local /inputs/ mirror when the requested dataset is present there, else the original upstream URL. The recipe writes it to the cache path, checksum-verifies it, makes it read-only, and copies it over the site-packages neurokit2/data/data.py, refusing to overwrite anything other than the pristine 0.2.13 loader (hash-checked). Only where the bytes are read from changes, not which bytes: the full-network pristine-loader run and the offline adapted run produced identical endpoint CSVs. A reference copy of the adapter is also kept at setup/data_read.py.

Dependency recipe only (no analysis edits): pyproject.toml declares neurokit2==0.2.13 plus its own runtime dependencies exactly as listed in its pyproject (matplotlib>=3.5.0, numpy>=2.0.0, pandas<3.0.0, PyWavelets>=1.4.0, requests, scikit-learn>=1.0.0, scipy, setuptools<82.0.0); system-packages.json is empty.
unresolved_assumptions: The scientific stack is pinned only at neurokit2==0.2.13; the transitive versions resolved by uv at test time were numpy 2.5.4, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.18.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1, matplotlib 3.11.2. A later test re-resolving newer minor versions could change low-order digits of the HRV indices.

Dataset provenance/redistribution: the recipe fetches bio_resting_5min_100hz.csv from the upstream NeuroKit GitHub data folder at staging time (network is available then) rather than redistributing it inside the bundle; the independent data-redistribution review noted in the preparation remains open, so the staged file's licensing status is still 'not established independently'.

The NaN columns observed (HRV_ULF, HRV_SDANN2, HRV_SDNNI2, HRV_SDANN5, HRV_SDNNI5) are NeuroKit 0.2.13's behaviour for a 5-minute recording; they are exported as empty CSV fields, and it cannot be confirmed from the unexecuted notebook (conversion reports executed=false, no stored outputs) whether the original author's environment produced the same empties, though the same package version and the same dataset are used here.

Matplotlib figures are rendered to an offscreen Agg canvas rather than displayed; the plots are retained (show=True calls execute) but nothing validates their visual content, since no figure was exported as an endpoint in the reviewed plan.
